The Field Converter framework operates by combining geometric initialization with temporal residual learning. Initially, camera and pitch geometry are used to compute an approximate 3D root position of each player via ray-ground intersection. This provides a coarse but metrically grounded starting point. Subsequently, a temporal refinement module processes this initial estimate along with visual and geometric cues to predict a residual correction. The refinement can be implemented using various architectures such as MLP, TCN, or Transformer. These models learn to correct the geometrically initialized root positions based on temporal context and image features. The process is iterative and improves localization accuracy significantly—reducing root error from 49 cm to below 15 cm. The final pose estimation is expressed in a shared world coordinate system, enabling accurate tracking and analysis of player movements. Failure occurs primarily during airborne motion where geometric initialization fails due to lack of ground contact. The framework's strength lies in its ability to leverage both spatial and temporal information to produce robust, world-grounded poses.
